BOTH INNER COUNTERS ARE RELOADED from their
targets (dmem[13], dmem[12]) at the top of
every pass. A version without the reloads
reads zero, subtracts one, wraps to 255, and
produces hundreds of thousands of clocks where
thousands were asked for - while looking
completely correct. 19 ms as NOPs would be

THE OUTER STEP IS NOT 4*n3 + 11. It is
Why the frame is a SLOT and not a delay.
The obvious implementation is "pulse 1.5 ms, then
wait 18.5 ms". That works until the position
changes: a forgotten subtraction turns 50 Hz into
45 Hz at one end of the travel and 58 Hz at the
other. A servo notices - the position jitters
So each position carries its OWN gap, chosen as
20 ms minus its own pulse, and the rise-to-rise
interval is 20 ms whatever the pulse is. The gap
is not "the rest of the frame", it is the frame
Why the order is a checkable property.
A sweep that only grows can be satisfied by a
firmware that emits the right widths in the wrong
order, and a testbench that sorts its
measurements before checking them cannot tell
Why two positions are a full 20 ms and three are not.
Positions 0 and 1 sit a full 20 ms apart so the
frame rate can be measured. Positions 2..4 use a
2.5 ms gap - a fifth of that - which saves 45 ms
of simulated time. The trade is stated rather
than hidden: the 50 Hz claim rests on the
MEASURED frame period, and the sweep claim rests
on five measured pulse WIDTHS, which is all it
needs. Nothing about the width measurement is
weakened by the short gaps, and the TB labels
the short ones "a short sweep gap, not a frame"
rather than pretending they are slots.
